title: GenWave Font Pack Manifest
description: The <slug>.font.json shape a GenWave station fetches for a kind:"font" catalog entry (app repo SPEC F104.1/F104.2, GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogFontManifest/CatalogFontManifestSerializer). Mirrors theme-manifest.schema.json's posture exactly: additionalProperties is true throughout, and this schema pins TYPES ONLY — it never rejects a byte-valid manifest over a field it doesn't yet know about or a value shape the app's own hardened deserializer (CatalogFontManifestSerializer.Deserialize) checks more strictly. That deserializer is the real validator (non-empty family/license/sourceUrl/subset, each files[] element's own role/file/weight/style/bytes checked present and positive); this schema only catches gross shape errors (wrong type, missing key) so a malformed catalog submission fails fast in CI rather than only at app fetch time. Never-reject-byte-valid: a manifest this schema accepts is not guaranteed to load in the app, but a manifest the app can actually load must never be rejected here for a reason the app itself doesn't enforce.
$comment: `files[].file`'s pattern ends in (?![\s\S]), the same portable absolute-end-of-string anchor schemas/index.schema.json documents in full and schemas/theme-meta.schema.json repeats — used here rather than a bare `$` for the same reason: Python's re `$` also matches immediately before a trailing newline, and `\Z` is Python-only (a literal 'Z' under ECMA-262). Repeated verbatim rather than by reference so this file stands alone.

family.description: Font-family name (CatalogFontManifest.Family) — matches the theme manifest's fonts.*.family when a shipped theme references this pack. Shape and length are byte-identical to schemas/index.schema.json's own optional shelf-card `family` field (GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.FamilyPattern/MaxFamilyLength) — the same CSS-injection-safe character set and 64-character cap — because CatalogFontManifestSerializer.Deserialize hands THIS value straight onto the wire's `FontFamily` field (CatalogController.ToEntryResponse reads `fontManifest?.Family` with no shape check of its own) the moment a station fetches the pack's detail view; this schema is the only gate a manifest's own `family` value gets, so it must be at least this strict rather than deferring to a check that lives only on the index's copy of the value.

files.description: 1-2 latin-subsetted faces (CatalogFontManifest.Files) — an upright face and, optionally, a second italic face; a font pack is one family, role-agnostic, never a full weight/style matrix (CatalogFontManifestFile's own remarks).

license.description: SPDX licence identifier (CatalogFontManifest.License), e.g. "OFL-1.1" — FONTS.md step 1's "OFL or an equivalent" confirm. tools/validate.py additionally checks this value against the catalog's own permitted-licence set; this schema pins presence and type only.

sourceUrl.description: Canonical upstream repository URL (CatalogFontManifest.SourceUrl) — FONTS.md step 1's "locate its canonical upstream repository"; FONTS.md's own step-2 provenance example (and this repo's golden.font.json parity fixture) always records one as `https://github.com/...`. Anchored to the scheme prefix only (not a full URL grammar) — enough to reject an `http://`, `javascript:`, or schemeless value without over-fitting a rule shape this schema doesn't otherwise validate.

version.description: Upstream tag/commit, when determinable (CatalogFontManifest.Version, FONTS.md step 2's provenance-record example: `"version": null, // upstream tag/commit, when determinable`). Null-tolerant on purpose — not every upstream exposes one.

subset.description: The subsetting step recorded (CatalogFontManifest.Subset), e.g. "latin" — FONTS.md step 3.

fontFile.description: One face inside `files[]` (CatalogFontManifestFile) — role-agnostic ("upright"/"italic"), not a full weight/style matrix. All five declared fields are required — this mirrors theme-manifest.schema.json's `fontAsset` posture exactly (full parity, not a split): CatalogFontManifestSerializer.Deserialize degrades the WHOLE manifest to null unless every files[] element's role/file/weight/style are present and non-empty and bytes is present and positive, the same all-fields-mandatory shape `fontAsset` (src/weight/style, all required) already has for the theme kind. This schema is at least as strict as that deserializer rather than deferring the rejection to app fetch time.

role.description: Which face this is within the pack, e.g. "upright" or "italic" (CatalogFontManifestFile.Role).

file.description: Bare filename (no path) of the vendored asset this face resolves to, e.g. "space-grotesk-variable-latin.woff2" (CatalogFontManifestFile.File) — the pack's sibling asset under the same entries/<slug>/ directory, never a path or URL. Same closed woff2 extension and bare-filename character set the app's own asset path pattern enforces (GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.AssetFileNameText, restricted here to woff2 since a manifest `file` always names a face, never the pack's OFL.txt).

weight.description: CSS font-weight descriptor, e.g. "300 700" for a variable face (CatalogFontManifestFile.Weight). Required and non-empty — CatalogFontManifestSerializer.Deserialize rejects the whole manifest on an empty/missing value.

bytes.description: Measured byte size of this face after subsetting (CatalogFontManifestFile.Bytes, FONTS.md step 4). Required and positive — CatalogFontManifestSerializer.Deserialize rejects the whole manifest on a missing/non-positive value; tools/validate.py separately enforces the summed per-pack ceiling over the entry's actual asset files on disk.
